title: Frontend: Even or odd
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Even or odd. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. Classify a safe integer as even or odd. Blank, fractional and unsafe input shows Invalid integer. Zero is even. Render controlled labelled inputs with these exact names: Number. A Calculate submit button computes the result. Render JSON.stringify(result) in [data-testid="result"]. Validation failure clears result and shows the documented message in [data-testid="error"].
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Reject blank and non-integer values before applying remainder.
alternativeApproaches: Add a BigInt mode and keep its parsing error messages separate from ordinary numeric input.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Zero; positive/negative integers; decimals.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
